trust_decision.summary: An archive streamed from the session target may be written only inside the session's local downloads directory: each member target path, each symlink/hardlink linkname and each special-file member is resolved and refused when it escapes that directory, and setuid/setgid bits are stripped, while owner-write is still forced; enforced in Session.download by wrapping tarfile's _extract_member before tar.extractall.

landing_point.why: the unconditional tar.extractall(local_download_folder) of the archive received from the target; the commit subject names download() tar extraction, and an engineer reading only the summary looks here

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI menu command 'download' (penelope.py:1038), CLI menu command 'open' (penelope.py:1056), MCP socket method 'download' (penelope.py:5877, driven by extras/mcp_penelope.py:264-272)
fix_sites.module_kind: session transfer method reached from CLI command handlers and a local unix-socket API

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Windows branch of the same method also unpacks a target-supplied archive into the downloads folder, but it uses zipfile on a different OS transport and Python's ZipFile.extract already discards '..' and absolute components, so a solver can reasonably argue that branch is not part of this tar advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The pre-existing wrapper forces every extracted member owner-writable (tarinfo.mode |= 0o200) and the agent transport legitimately packs symlinks as symlinks, so legitimate downloads contain internal relative links; a blanket link refusal, a switch to tarfile.data_filter, or dropping the mode wrapper breaks valid downloads and loses the writable-mode guarantee.

O6_input_shapes: dot-dot traversal in the member name, including nested a/../../x
symlink member whose linkname resolves outside the destination
hardlink member whose linkname resolves outside the destination
special-file members: only isreg/isdir/issym/islnk are extracted, fifo/device entries are refused
setuid/setgid mode bits cleared on every member while owner-write is preserved

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject member names containing '..' or starting with '/' before extractall, which keeps add_w but misses absolute-link symlink/hardlink members, the resolved-target distinction, and special-file entries.

out_of_scope_notes: penelope.py:3458-3463 with do_open (penelope.py:1056-1069) trusts the target's readlink output: a reported path like '/../../x' makes local_path escape the downloads folder and is then handed to xdg-open (local file open, not the archive write this advisory covers).

penelope.py:3825-3835: script() writes a URL-derived filename (prefix + filename) straight into the session scripts folder with no name validation - a separate local-write naming issue, not archive extraction.
unverified: The CPython stdlib was not readable from this sandbox, so the claim that ZipFile.extract strips '..' and absolute components (why penelope.py:3507-3511 is not a traversal route) rests on stdlib knowledge, not on a file:line in this tree.
